Definition: from G4862 and G5162 (in a passive sense); a fellow-nursling, i.e. comrade:--brought up with.
BiblicalUsage: In the church at Antioch there are certain prophets and teachers, as Barnabas, and Simeon called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul. Manaen is the fellow-nursling, brought up with Herod, and the church that holds a man raised beside a king is the church that sends Saul and Barnabas to the nations.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that God can raise a man beside a king and call him to the church, and I hold that Manaen's place in Antioch is the proof that no upbringing is wasted in God's hands.
